proposal.hypothesis: A two-group scalar unroll may expose independent table-lookup chains and amortize loop control compared with the measured scalar baseline (three samples, mean 55.0005 µs), while preserving the original one-group path for tails and invalid input. Register pressure and added control may negate any benefit; no speedup is assumed.

retained: Unrolled the safe decode loop by two eight-character groups when at least 21 input bytes remain, loading and looking up both groups before committing output.

Preserved fallback semantics: if the first group is invalid, leave it for bytewise processing; if only the second is invalid, commit the first group and resume at the second. Retained the original single-group loop for remaining safe blocks.
Used scalar operations only; did not add SIMD, threading, or benchmark-size specialization.

proposal.hypothesis: A scalar two-group unroll can expose independent table lookups to the processor and halve loop-control frequency relative to a single eight-character group. Requiring 20 remaining characters reads only the two complete groups while leaving a quartet for scalar padding/tail handling. There are no candidate timings yet; the baseline is correct at about 55.0 µs mean, and h01's two-group attempt failed to build because line separators were emitted as literal escape sequences.

retained: Interleave scalar table lookups from two independent eight-character groups and decode 16 input characters to 12 output bytes per bulk iteration.
Keep a 20-character remaining-input guard so the bulk loop reads only complete unpadded groups; decode padding and the tail quartet scalarly.
Retain scalar execution only, without explicit SIMD or parallel work.
